visual_description:
1. The page presents three successive StarDist-related figure groups embedded in a document: Figure 28 at the top compares a training image with its mask; Figure 29 compares representative training and test images; and the partially visible Figure 30 at the bottom begins an analysis of detected bubble features with an outlined-image panel and a size-distribution plot. A section heading and explanatory paragraph separate Figures 29 and 30.

2. Figure 28 contains two side-by-side panels. Panel (a) is a grayscale microscopy image containing many overlapping bubbles or approximately elliptical objects of different sizes. Panel (b) is the corresponding instance mask: each detected object is represented by a separate colored region against a dark-purple background, allowing adjacent bubbles to be distinguished.

3. The caption below the first pair reads: “Figure 28. Training image (a) and mask (b) samples for the StarDist method.” The panel labels “(a)” and “(b)” are centered below their respective images.

4. Figure 29 also contains two side-by-side panels labeled “(a)” and “(b).” Both are color microscopy images containing numerous bubble-like objects with varying shapes, sizes, and intensities. Panel (a) is identified as a sample from the training data, whereas panel (b) is identified as a sample from the test data.

5. The visible portion of the second caption reads: “Figure 29. StarDist method application: sample image from training (a) and test (b) …”; the end of the caption is cropped from the image.

6. Below Figure 29, the italic section heading reads “4.3. Analysis of Bubble Features Obtained from the Trained StarDist Model.” The accompanying text explains that the StarDist result is a label image and/or a list of regions representing bubbles. These outputs are used to calculate the total number of bubbles per frame and obtain information about them using the scikit module [37].

7. The paragraph further states that bubble boundaries can be obtained from the individual mask by generalizing bounding polygons that contain sets of non-zero pixels. At this stage, information is acquired about each bubble’s center of mass and the coordinates of its boundary with another phase. It then refers to Figure 30b as showing a calculated distribution after applying StarDist and states that the resulting masks provide bubble characteristics including eccentricity and perimeter, among others. It also refers to Figure 31b as showing calculated eccentricities for the approximated objects; portions of several lines are cropped at the page edges.

8. The visible part of Figure 30 contains two panels. The left panel is a grayscale bubble image overlaid with orange contours around detected bubble boundaries, illustrating the instance outlines produced from the StarDist mask. Objects range from small near-circular regions to larger elongated or irregular bubbles.

9. The right panel is a histogram of bubble area or size. Its horizontal axis is labeled “Square [pixels]” and extends from approximately 0 to 6000 pixels; its vertical axis is labeled “Probability.” Blue histogram bars are concentrated at low square-pixel values and generally decline as size increases, producing a strongly right-skewed distribution. A smooth blue density curve follows the same pattern, peaking at a low size value and then decreasing toward zero. A few sparse bars remain at large values, including near 4000 and about 5800 pixels, indicating rare large bubbles. A small value “0.175” appears near the upper-left side of the plot area.
